sources.title: GLM-5.3-Flash: How to Run Locally - unsloth.ai
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash, also known as ox-alpha, is Z.ai's new 320B parameter (18B active) multimodal open model which outperforms GLM-5.2 across benchmarks and real-world tasks at one-tenth the price. GLM-5.3-Flash is the smaller version of GLM-5.3 and rivals Claude Opus 4.8 on coding and agentic benchmarks.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 - How to Run Locally | Unsloth Documentation
sources.snippet: The model has a 1M context window and can now run locally via Unsloth Dynamic GGUFs with llama.cpp or Unsloth Desktop. GLM-5.3-Flash Guide GLM-5.3 Guide If you want to run GLM-5.3-Flash, please read our specific article for it. Dynamic 1-bit GGUF reaches ~76% top-1 accuracy while being 85% smaller.

sources.title: How to Run GLM-5.3-Flash Locally: GGUF, Hardware and Benchmarks
sources.snippet: GLM-5.3-Flash is the first natively multimodal model in Z.ai's GLM-5 series, and the first one that's realistic to run locally: it has 320B total parameters and 18B active per token. This guide covers what the model is, how it performs in the benchmarks, how much memory you'll need to run it, and what your options are for running it today.
